image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on golden-yellow rippled water. The duck features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow bill, and a grey/brown body. It is positioned in the left-center of the frame, facing right.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a yellowish-green hue consistent with a mallard drake.
The eye is visible as a small dark spot on the side of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is compact and sits low in the water, appearing buoyant and streamlined.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, white neck ring, and greyish body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is swimming; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded by the water and body angle.
The folded wing structure is visible on the side of the body, appearing broad and consistent with duck anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear of the duck, appearing short and slightly upturned/curled, characteristic of a drake.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The iridescent green head has a slightly uniform, plastic-like sheen lacking the fine individual feather texture expected in high-resolution photography, though it mimics the general look of mallard plumage.
The interaction between the duck's hull and the water ripples is slightly soft; the displacement of water feels minimally physical, suggesting slight generative smoothing at the boundary.
